facts.value: c. 988, baptism of Vladimir of Kiev

citations.locator: Russian Orthodox Church (Moscow Patriarchate), member profile
citations.excerpt: About 988 the Emperor Vladimir was baptized, and he established Christianity as the official religion in his dominions.
Originally, he brought priests from the Byzantine empire and established a Greek hierarchy under a metropolitan.
The Patriarchate of Moscow was created in 1589 by Jeremias II, Patriarch of Constantinople.

facts.value: The Orthodox church of Russia. Its patriarchate, created in 1589, was replaced by a holy synod under Peter the Great and restored by the council of 1917 to 1918.

citations.excerpt: Peter the Great (1676 - 1725) abolished the office of patriarch and replaced it with the holy synod
In 1917-18 a large council of bishops, parish clergy and laity met in Moscow and initiated a thorough reorganization of all aspects of church life, in particular restoring the Patriarchate.

facts.value_before_verify: The autocephalous Orthodox church of Russia and neighboring countries. Its patriarchate dates from 1589, was replaced by a synod under Peter the Great and restored in 1917 to 1918.
